labels.label: T-abs-gluing-hausdorff/1-pushout-iff
labels.notes: Marked, closed: correct. DEFINITION. IsCorrespondingBoundaryPair j₁ j₂ x y (GluingHausdorff.lean:132-134) is x ∈ frontier (range j₁) ∧ y ∈ frontier (range j₂) ∧ ∀ V ∈ 𝓝 x, ∀ V' ∈ 𝓝 y, ∃ w, j₁ w ∈ V ∧ j₂ w ∈ V'. With W = U, j₁ the inclusion and j₂ = ψ, this is Sbierski's Def 3.5 exactly as printed: p ∈ ∂U, p' ∈ ∂ψ(U), and ψ⁻¹(V' ∩ ψ(U)) ∩ V ≠ ∅ for all neighbourhoods V, V'. Sources: the PDF, page 15, rendered and read, and Maximal_GHD2.tex:531. Since U is open, frontier U = closure U \ U = ∂U. The boundary memberships are included, so the notion is the same, not weaker: without them every graph pair (j₁ w, j₂ w) would qualify and the iff would fail. STATEMENT. t2Space_iff_forall_not_isCorrespondingBoundaryPair (:305): [T2Space X] [T2Space Y], j₁, j₂ open embeddings of an arbitrary space W ⊢ T2Space (Gluing j₁ j₂) ↔ ∀ x y, ¬ IsCorrespondingBoundaryPair. Gluing (Pushout.lean:84-95) is Quot of X ⊕ Y by j₁ w ~ j₂ w with the quotient topology, i.e. Sbierski's M̃ and Chruściel's (M1 ⊔ M2)/Ψ_O. The Hausdorff pieces are carried from all three sources, and the hypothesis-free form t2Space_iff_t2Space_and_forall_not_isCorrespondingBoundaryPair (:314) removes even that. Lean ≥ title. Sbierski proves only the ⇐ direction, so the iff is stronger. The hypothesis is satisfiable, and lineTwoOrigins_isCorrespondingBoundaryPair gives an inhabitant of the predicate. The supporting equivalences check out: the closure of the graph, one filter, one sequence under first countability, and Cdist for Hausdorff pieces. The 'one net' form named in the docstring prose (:51) is not stated in Lean; SCOPE (:96) discloses this. The closer's finding on the Def 3.5 formula is false (major finding 1), but the reading the closer used is the paper's own formula, so the definition is faithful.

labels.label: T-abs-gluing-hausdorff/2-family
labels.notes: Marked, closed: correct. FamilyGlueData (CBG/FamilyGluing.lean:168-180) is standard gluing data: open U i j ⊆ M i, continuous φ i j : U i j → M j landing in U j i, U i i = ⊤, φ i i = id, and the cocycle. The cocycle with indices (j, i, k) gives t_ij(U_ij ∩ U_ik) ⊆ U_jk; with φ_φ it is the usual condition, so it is not vacuous. tHomeo makes each φ i j an open embedding (isOpenEmbedding_φ), which matches 'glued along open embeddings' and Sbierski's (3.15). t2Space_iff_forall_not_isCorrespondingBoundaryPair (:568) quantifies over all ordered pairs (i, j). The case i = j is vacuous, since frontier ⊤ = ∅. It instantiates the two-space notion at (Subtype.val : U i j → M i, φ i j), the MCGHD U_{ik} with ψ_{ik} in Sbierski's notation. The hypothesis-free form (:577) drops [∀ i, T2Space (M i)]. t2Space_of_directed (:610) needs only Hausdorff pieces and 'any two members embed wholly in a third'. t2Space_of_total (:635) is Graf–Ling Lemma 29's 'N_α ≲ N_β or N_β ≲ N_α'. Graf–Ling's Lemma 24 (graf2023uniqueness.txt:968-985) shows the ψ_αβ have open images, so their setting fits FamilyGlueData. Chruściel's chain union (:345-357) also fits as U α β = ⊤ for α ≤ β. No added hypothesis.

labels.label: T-abs-gluing-hausdorff/3-closed-nonhausdorff
labels.notes: Unmarked and partial, which is correct. nonHausdorffPoints Z = {z | ∃ z' ≠ z, ¬ Disjoint (𝓝 z) (𝓝 z')} (:111), proved equivalent to ¬T2 (:114). nonHausdorffLeft = ι₁⁻¹' nonHausdorffPoints (Gluing j₁ j₂) (:329) is Chruściel's H verbatim: 'the set of non-Hausdorff points p in M1, thus p′ = i_{M1}(p) ≡ [p] is non-Hausdorff in M′' (chrusciel2013maximal.txt:877-879). It is not some other set. COUNTEREXAMPLE. Checked by hand and kernel-checked. X = Y = ℝ², W = (0,∞)×ℝ, j₁(a,c) = (a, eᶜ), j₂ = inclusion; both are open embeddings, and X, Y are Hausdorff. The closure of the graph consists of the limits of ((a_n, e^{c_n}), (a_n, c_n)); convergence of the Y side forces c_n → c finite. So the boundary pairs are exactly ((0, eᶜ), (0, c)), giving H = {0} × (0,∞), and (0,0) ∈ closure H \ H. (0,0) lies in ∂O_X, so H is closed neither in X nor in ∂O_X. The title's assertion 3 is therefore false as pure topology, in the X-side reading and in the gluing reading (not_isClosed_nonHausdorffPoints_expGluing). The finding is correctly scoped. It says Chruściel's justification 'by elementary topology … (as its complement is open)' is invalid. It does not say his Lemma 3.3 is false: the REPORT says that under maximality and global hyperbolicity the question is unsettled. The use at :900-903 ('p* ∈ … consequently Γ ∈ Y' needs p* ∈ H) and the compactness at :996-1000 were both verified. The true forms are correct and unmarked. isClosed_correspondingPairs has no hypothesis, and the pairs set is ETT's literal C intersected with ∂j₁(N) × ∂j₂(N) (ETT.tex:2012, 2240-2242). isClosed_nonHausdorffLeft_of_isCompact has a satisfiable hypothesis (Y compact suffices). SHEAR. Also checked by hand: shearLeft(a,c) = (a, ac) has closure-of-graph pairs ((0,0), (0,c)) for every c, and C = {(0,0)}, which is not open in ∂U = {0}×ℝ. shearGluing_not_isOpen_in_frontier states non-openness in the subspace topology correctly. Both shear findings are framed as 'not topological; proved from geometry in the source' (Sbierski :724, :787-788; ETT.tex:2240). They do not claim the papers are wrong, which is true and appropriately worded.

findings.what: FALSE FINDING. The REPORT states as fact that Sbierski's Def 3.5 'writes the condition as psi^{-1}V' ∩ psi(U) ∩ V ≠ ∅, which does not typecheck as written', and that the formula repeated at :1078 is the same typo. Both are wrong. The published formula is ψ⁻¹(V′ ∩ ψ(U)) ∩ V ≠ ∅. Evidence: page 15 of references/sbierski/pdf/sbierski2013existence.pdf, rendered and read; the arXiv LaTeX the dispatch named, papers/sbierski-mghd/legacy/labeled/Maximal_GHD2.tex:531 `\psi^{-1}\big( V' \cap \psi(U)\big) \cap V \neq \emptyset`; and the same at :751. pdftotext dropped the \big( \big) delimiters, which are cmex glyphs: the -bbox output shows empty 5 pt and 7 pt gaps exactly where they sit. The closer's 'reading' is the paper's own formula, so the Lean definition is unaffected. Only the claim of an error in the paper is false, and it would reach the author as a fact. The other half of the finding is genuine: at :1077 / Maximal_GHD2.tex:751 'V′ of p′' is written for the point called q.

findings.what: The proposal says Causal.CBG.Corresponding.Corresponds 'is the same notion in (U, psi) form'. Corresponds (Corresponding.lean:263-265, docstring 'Sbierski Def 3.5, the relation') is only the neighbourhood condition ∀ O ∈ 𝓝 p, ∀ O' ∈ 𝓝 q, ∃ x ∈ U, x ∈ O ∧ ψ x ∈ O'. It lacks the memberships p ∈ ∂U and q ∈ ∂ψ(U), which callers there pass separately as hypotheses. Graph points satisfy it, so it is not the same predicate as IsCorrespondingBoundaryPair. The claim that the module transitively imports models is correct.
findings.fix: In the kb entry, say 'Corresponds is the neighbourhood condition of Def 3.5 (without the ∂ memberships), in (U, ψ) form'.
